newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iraqi Kurds agree on ceasefire, Iran says.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurds agree on ceasefire, Iran says.

text.p: Senior officials of two Iraqi Kurdish groups have agreed at talks in Iran on a ceasefire to end recent clashes in northern Iraq, the official Iranian news agency IRNA reported on Wednesday.

It said representatives from the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) and the Kurdistan Islamic Movement agreed at the end of talks on Tuesday night in Tehran on the "need to hold onto the ceasefire" reached on Monday.

IRNA quoted a joint statement as saying the two sides agreed "negotiations should continue until the complete cessation of all hostilities and return to normalcy and mutual cooperation which will guarantee the interests of the people of Iraqi Kurdistan."
It said the talks, held at the invitation of Iran, laid the "preliminary grounds for final agreements between the heads of the two parties".
The PUK said on Monday it had clashed with the Islamic Movement in northern Iraq near the Iranian border at the weekend as part of sporadic fighting that broke out earlier in April.
It said its traditional rival the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) was supporting the Islamist group.
The KDP and PUK have met frequently for peace talks in Turkey since they declared a ceasefire last October following intense fighting.
Kurdish rebels have been in control of northern Iraq since Baghdad's defeat in the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait.
